title: Altered cortical thickness following prenatal sodium valproate exposure.
ehr_evidence: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were acquired on the 3T Siemens Magnetom Trio at Murdoch Childrens Research Institute, Melbourne, using a 12-channel coil.
summary: Neuroimaging study comparing cortical thickness and verbal abilities in 16 children prenatally exposed to valproate versus 16 matched controls.
key_findings: Increased cortical thickness in left inferior frontal gyrus and left medial occipital cortex (P < 0.05, corrected).
Significant interaction between group and hemispheric thickness in inferior frontal region (F(1, 29) = 12.38, P = 0.001), showing absence of normal right-left asymmetry in exposed children.
VPA dose significantly correlated with right inferior frontal gyrus thickness (r = 0.57, P = 0.02).
No significant correlation between VPA dose and left inferior frontal gyrus thickness (r = -0.17, P = 0.53).
No significant difference in total cortical white and grey matter between groups (both P > 0.1).
Trend towards poorer verbal abilities and greater left inferior frontal gyrus thickness in exposed children (r = -0.42, P = 0.12).
population: 16 children (mean age 7.2 years) prenatally exposed to valproate and 16 age- and sex-matched controls (mean age 8.1 years)
limitations: limited dose range (relatively low average dose)
